children: BTCUSD plunged, triggering over $2.4B in liquidations—85–93% longs. Single sessions liquidated 100k–180k traders. Crypto market cap dropped about $110B in 36 hours.
Around the 10/10 anniversary, BTCUSD spot CFD saw over $600M liquidated in one hour — the biggest hourly wipeout in a month; overall market leverage was lighter than the previous anniversary.
BTCUSD spot ETFs saw heavy U.S. outflows in early October: Oct 7 withdrawals about $487M (largest since June), leaving October net outflows near $165M, then easing to $244M.
BTCUSD total open futures exposure dropped from ~$154B to ~$142B, showing a net reduction in aggregate positions while leverage dynamics persist.
BTCUSD spot around $82,699 (+0.14% 24h), about 35% below Oct 2025 peak ~$126,000. Glassnode shows leveraged position cluster near $75,000, marking OI concentration.
55,600 BTC from short-term holders moved to exchanges at a loss; BTCUSD spot CFD open interest stayed near $150B, while recent liquidity stress was likened to an October 2025 $19B liquidation event.
BTCUSD slid toward $81,000; $83,000 cited as key bullish level. Traders eye 50-week MA near $78,000 and multiple weekly closes below $78,000 as risk signals.
After a Oct 10, 2025 tariff threat, reports say over $19B forced liquidations. In the following week traders cut BTCUSD risk to avoid similar forced closures, per market commentary.
BTCUSD spot CFD volatility eased from ~84% (2018) to ~46% now, yet 2024 shows 10 extreme intraday three-sigma moves; macro shocks and derivatives positioning linked to abrupt moves.
Corporate entities bought 193,000 BTC year-to-date in 2026; total corporate holdings about 1.64M BTC (7.8% supply). Two firms acquired 197,000 BTC combined; one firm holds 848,000 BTC.
